set_d.instruction: Directions: Read the following passage carefully and answer the questions given below.
set_d.passage:
The investigation by The Indian Express into the Election Commission of India’s (ECI) functioning during its Special Intensive Revision (SIR) shows that the disquiet over what transpired under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s watch is not limited to civil society, the media and the Opposition. It ran through the ECI itself, as Election Commissioners (EC) Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi objected on record at least 14 times between October 2025 and August 2026 to decisions, many of which, they said, were taken without their knowledge. Their dissent mirrors what many have long said about the SIR. In May, Mr. Joshi had warned that Form 6, the application for new electors, could not be altered without the government amending the rules. Yet, in July, the form contained questions on whether the applicants or their parents or grandparents figured in the “electoral roll of the last SIR”, which Mr. Sandhu called “unauthorised and illegal”. The ECs also flagged the centralisation of the electoral roll database, sought an audit, and recorded that field officials lacked complete access to the ERONet portal. This mirrors what local election officials had complained of: that many of the changes in the rolls were done at the central database level overriding Electoral Registration Officers, the statutory authority on voters’ eligibility.

The consequences of the anomalies in the ECI’s decision-making and its functioning were the deepest in West Bengal. About 60 lakh electors were flagged for software-generated “logical discrepancies” — many were dubious — and 27 lakh names were deleted. Of the 38 lakh appeals pending before tribunals, 16.1 lakh were by those seeking to remove voters whom judicial officers had included; Mr. Sandhu’s question of who authorised filing them on the ECI’s behalf remains unanswered. Meanwhile, over nine in 10 appeals against deletion decided so far have restored the electors, which suggests that the exercise struck off lakhs of genuine voters before the West Bengal elections. The Hindu’s analysis also revealed that 24 of the 70 seats in Delhi now have fewer electors in draft rolls than those who actually voted just a year and a half ago. On Wednesday, Justice Dipankar Datta, as part of a two-judge Bench, held in his opinion that the 2023 Act’s replacement of the CJI, whom the Anoop Baranwal judgment had placed on the selection panel, with a Union Minister, fails the “perception test”. It was this panel that chose Mr. Kumar as CEC. Regrettably, the Supreme Court had earlier upheld the SIR without adequately confronting its design, which deletes electors before verification and places the burden of proving eligibility on the citizen rather than the state, thereby defeating the constitutional guarantee of universal adult franchise. Mr. Kumar must resign and the Court must halt further deletions until the roll database is audited. Anything less will be a defeat for India’s democracy.

questions.question: What is the author's central argument?
options: Judicial officers filed 16.1 lakh tribunal appeals to remove validly registered electors without obtaining permission from the Supreme Court.
Local election officials bypassed the central database by unilaterally deleting 27 lakh voters in West Bengal without tribunal approval.
The Supreme Court intentionally subverted democratic principles by replacing the Chief Justice of India with a Union Minister on the selection panel.
The flawed design and procedural internal irregularities of the SIR undermine universal adult franchise, necessitating the CEC's resignation and an immediate audit.
questions.correct_answer: The flawed design and procedural internal irregularities of the SIR undermine universal adult franchise, necessitating the CEC's resignation and an immediate audit.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'The flawed design and procedural internal irregularities of the SIR undermine universal adult franchise, necessitating the CEC's resignation and an immediate audit.' is correct:** The author details internal dissent within the ECI, procedural lapses, and massive improper voter deletions, concluding that CEC Gyanesh Kumar must resign and deletions must be halted until an audit is conducted to safeguard democracy.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Local election officials bypassed the central database by unilaterally deleting 27 lakh voters in West Bengal without tribunal approval.': This misattributes the deletions to local officials, whereas the passage states changes were made at the central database level overriding statutory local officers.
• 'Judicial officers filed 16.1 lakh tribunal appeals to remove validly registered electors without obtaining permission from the Supreme Court.': The passage notes 16.1 lakh appeals were filed on the ECI's behalf to remove voters whom judicial officers had included, misassigning the action to judicial officers.
• 'The Supreme Court intentionally subverted democratic principles by replacing the Chief Justice of India with a Union Minister on the selection panel.': The passage states the replacement was done by the 2023 Act enacted by Parliament, not an intentional act of subversion by the Supreme Court itself.

questions.question: What can be reasonably inferred from the passage?
options: Form 6 was modified after the government officially amended the relevant statutory rules in May 2026.
Over nine in 10 appeals against deletion were restored, proving that software algorithms must be completely banned from electoral processes.
A high percentage of voter deletions under the SIR in West Bengal were erroneous and unjustifiable.
All 70 seats in Delhi experienced a drop in draft electoral roll numbers compared to actual voter turnout in the previous election.
questions.correct_answer: A high percentage of voter deletions under the SIR in West Bengal were erroneous and unjustifiable.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'A high percentage of voter deletions under the SIR in West Bengal were erroneous and unjustifiable.' is correct:** The passage states that over nine in 10 decided appeals against deletion restored the electors, which strongly implies that most deletions were unfounded.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Over nine in 10 appeals against deletion were restored, proving that software algorithms must be completely banned from electoral processes.': While the restoration statistic is correct detail, drawing the sweeping conclusion that software algorithms must be completely banned is unwarranted.
• 'Form 6 was modified after the government officially amended the relevant statutory rules in May 2026.': The passage indicates Form 6 was altered without the government amending the rules, making it unauthorised and illegal.
• 'All 70 seats in Delhi experienced a drop in draft electoral roll numbers compared to actual voter turnout in the previous election.': The passage specifies that 24 of the 70 seats in Delhi had fewer electors, not all 70 seats.

questions.question: Which assumption is necessary for the author's argument to hold?
options: Restoring voter eligibility through tribunal appeals after disenfranchisement is insufficient to prevent democratic damage if genuine voters are deleted prior to elections.
Logical discrepancies generated by software are inherently incapable of identifying any genuinely invalid voter records.
Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi were the only two officials aware of the administrative discrepancies in West Bengal.
Form 6 alterations were the sole factor responsible for the deletion of 27 lakh voter names in West Bengal.
questions.correct_answer: Restoring voter eligibility through tribunal appeals after disenfranchisement is insufficient to prevent democratic damage if genuine voters are deleted prior to elections.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Restoring voter eligibility through tribunal appeals after disenfranchisement is insufficient to prevent democratic damage if genuine voters are deleted prior to elections.' is correct:** The author argues that deleting voters prior to verification defeats universal adult franchise, assuming that post-facto appeals do not mitigate the harm caused before an election.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi were the only two officials aware of the administrative discrepancies in West Bengal.': This is an overly restrictive under-generalisation that is not necessary for the author's systemic argument.
• 'Form 6 alterations were the sole factor responsible for the deletion of 27 lakh voter names in West Bengal.': The author attributes deletions to software-generated logical discrepancies and central database overrides, not solely Form 6.
• 'Logical discrepancies generated by software are inherently incapable of identifying any genuinely invalid voter records.': The author calls many discrepancies dubious, but does not need to assume that software can never identify invalid records.

questions.question:
Consider statements (I), (II), and (III). Which are correct according to the passage?

(I) Election Commissioners Sandhu and Joshi formally dissented at least 14 times regarding decisions taken without their knowledge.
(II) Electoral Registration Officers are the statutory authority regarding voters' eligibility.
(III) The Supreme Court immediately halted all voter deletions and ordered a complete audit of the ERONet database.
options: Only (I) and (III)
(I), (II), and (III)
Only (I) and (II)
Only (II) and (III)
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Only (I) and (II)' is correct:** Statement (I) is directly stated (Sandhu and Joshi objected on record at least 14 times), and statement (II) is directly stated (Electoral Registration Officers, the statutory authority on voters' eligibility).

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Only (I) and (III)': Statement (III) is false because the passage explicitly states the Supreme Court upheld the SIR without confronting its design; the author is requesting the Court to halt deletions now.
• 'Only (II) and (III)': Statement (III) is an exaggerated false claim, making options containing (III) incorrect.
• '(I), (II), and (III)': Statement (III) is an exaggerated claim as the Supreme Court has not yet halted deletions or ordered an audit.

questions.question: What is the meaning of the phrase 'perception test' as used in the passage?
options: The standard that an appointment process must not only be fair but must also appear impartial and unbiased to the public.
A technical measure evaluated by software to determine voter perceptions of election integrity.
A broad policy requirement that all administrative electoral decisions must be submitted to public opinion surveys before implementation.
A constitutional directive mandating that selection panels consist exclusively of sitting judicial officers.
questions.correct_answer: The standard that an appointment process must not only be fair but must also appear impartial and unbiased to the public.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'The standard that an appointment process must not only be fair but must also appear impartial and unbiased to the public.' is correct:** In the context of Justice Datta's opinion regarding replacing the CJI with a Union Minister on the selection panel, the phrase refers to whether the process appears fair and independent from executive influence.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'A broad policy requirement that all administrative electoral decisions must be submitted to public opinion surveys before implementation.': This over-generalises a specific judicial concept regarding panel composition into a broad claim about public polling for all administrative decisions.
• 'A technical measure evaluated by software to determine voter perceptions of election integrity.': The passage connects the phrase to the 2023 Act's panel structure, not to software measurements.
• 'A constitutional directive mandating that selection panels consist exclusively of sitting judicial officers.': The passage mentions the CJI was previously on a multi-member panel, not that panels must consist exclusively of judges.

questions.question: The author's conclusion is most vulnerable to which criticism?
options: It presumes without evidence that Electoral Registration Officers have never committed administrative errors in voter registration.
It assumes that replacing the Chief Election Commissioner and auditing the database will resolve procedural flaws, without addressing whether broader constitutional remedies are needed.
It relies on the assumption that software-generated logical discrepancies can never be refined or corrected.
It over-generalizes that every single electoral process across all democratic nations is inherently corrupt and beyond repair.
questions.correct_answer: It assumes that replacing the Chief Election Commissioner and auditing the database will resolve procedural flaws, without addressing whether broader constitutional remedies are needed.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'It assumes that replacing the Chief Election Commissioner and auditing the database will resolve procedural flaws, without addressing whether broader constitutional remedies are needed.' is correct:** The author demands individual resignation and an audit as the solution, which may be vulnerable to the criticism that systemic design flaws in the law require deeper structural reform beyond personnel changes.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'It over-generalizes that every single electoral process across all democratic nations is inherently corrupt and beyond repair.': This distractor presents an absurd over-generalisation not advocated by the author, who specifically focuses on the ECI's SIR.
• 'It presumes without evidence that Electoral Registration Officers have never committed administrative errors in voter registration.': The author focuses on central overrides of statutory officers, not on claiming local officers are infallible.
• 'It relies on the assumption that software-generated logical discrepancies can never be refined or corrected.': The author criticises dubious discrepancies and central overrides, not the theoretical future capability of software.

questions.question: The evidence in the passage lends the greatest support to:
options: The centralisation of the electoral roll database undermined the statutory authority of local Electoral Registration Officers.
Justice Dipankar Datta's opinion led to the immediate reinstatement of the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel.
The Supreme Court has decided to overturn the 2023 Act following public protests.
Field officials deliberately sabotaged the ERONet portal to prevent central database updates.
questions.correct_answer: The centralisation of the electoral roll database undermined the statutory authority of local Electoral Registration Officers.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'The centralisation of the electoral roll database undermined the statutory authority of local Electoral Registration Officers.' is correct:** The passage explicitly states that centralisation overridden Electoral Registration Officers, who are the statutory authority on voters' eligibility, and field officials lacked access.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Justice Dipankar Datta's opinion led to the immediate reinstatement of the Chief Justice of India on the selection panel.': This is a plausible-sounding but unsupported inference, as the passage only notes Justice Datta expressed an opinion in a judgment.
• 'Field officials deliberately sabotaged the ERONet portal to prevent central database updates.': The passage states field officials lacked complete access to the portal, not that they sabotaged it.
• 'The Supreme Court has decided to overturn the 2023 Act following public protests.': The passage does not state that the Court overturned the Act or that public protests drove court actions.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a logical extension of the author's reasoning?
options: Software algorithms must be completely eliminated from all election management tasks.
All tribunal appeals regarding voter inclusion should be dismissed automatically if filed on behalf of the Election Commission.
Form 6 should be permanently abolished because it contained unauthorized questions about applicants' ancestors.
Electoral revision procedures should place the burden of proof on the state to verify ineligibility before removing any citizen from the electoral rolls.
questions.correct_answer: Electoral revision procedures should place the burden of proof on the state to verify ineligibility before removing any citizen from the electoral rolls.
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Electoral revision procedures should place the burden of proof on the state to verify ineligibility before removing any citizen from the electoral rolls.' is correct:** The author explicitly criticises the SIR design for deleting electors before verification and placing the burden on citizens, extending logically to the view that the state must bear the burden of verification first.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Form 6 should be permanently abolished because it contained unauthorized questions about applicants' ancestors.': This misinterprets the passage fact; the author objected to illegal additions to Form 6 without rule amendments, not to the existence of Form 6 itself.
• 'Software algorithms must be completely eliminated from all election management tasks.': This is an extreme position that goes beyond the author's critique of dubious software-generated discrepancies and central overrides.
• 'All tribunal appeals regarding voter inclusion should be dismissed automatically if filed on behalf of the Election Commission.': The author questions who authorised filing them, but does not argue for automatic dismissal without due process.

questions.question: Choose the word most similar in meaning in this context to 'disquiet':
options: Mild excitement
Absolute hostility
Quiet satisfaction
Apprehension
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Apprehension' is correct:** In the passage, 'disquiet' refers to the grave anxiety, concern, or unease surrounding the ECI's functioning, which matches 'apprehension'.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Mild excitement': This is a partially true/incorrect statement that misinterprets 'disquiet' as positive or enthusiastic emotion.
• 'Absolute hostility': This overstates 'disquiet', which means anxiety or unease rather than active, violent hatred.
• 'Quiet satisfaction': This is an antonym, describing contentment rather than worry or concern.

questions.question: What is the overall tone of the passage?
options: Mildly informative
Critical and urgent
Wholly indifferent
Unconditionally supportive
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Critical and urgent' is correct:** The author sharply criticises the ECI's actions, highlights serious democratic threats, and urgently calls for the CEC's resignation and an immediate halt to deletions.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'Mildly informative': This under-generalises and trivialize the passage's strong condemnatory and alarming stance as merely neutral information.
• 'Wholly indifferent': The author expresses deep concern for democratic rights, contradicting indifference.
• 'Unconditionally supportive': The passage censures the ECI and CEC, making supportive tone incorrect.

questions.question: What is the most appropriate title for the passage?
options: The Total Collapse of Democracy: How India Lost Its Fundamental Right to Vote Forever
The History of Supreme Court Decisions on Electoral Selection Committees
Electoral Registration Officers and the ERONet Portal: A Technical Review
Undermining the Franchise: Internal Dissent and Systemic Flaws in the ECI
questions.correct_answer: Undermining the Franchise: Internal Dissent and Systemic Flaws in the ECI
questions.explanation:
**Why 'Undermining the Franchise: Internal Dissent and Systemic Flaws in the ECI' is correct:** This title accurately encompasses both the internal objections by ECs and the systemic procedural flaws affecting voter franchise discussed throughout the text.

**Why other options are incorrect:**
• 'The Total Collapse of Democracy: How India Lost Its Fundamental Right to Vote Forever': This is an exaggerated claim that overstates the passage's warning into a definitive, permanent doom.
• 'Electoral Registration Officers and the ERONet Portal: A Technical Review': This is too narrow as it focuses only on one specific administrative aspect mentioned in the text.
• 'The History of Supreme Court Decisions on Electoral Selection Committees': This is too narrow as it focuses only on the legal selection panel detail mentioned near the end.
